definitions.explanation: A sweet confection, typically hard candy made from sugar. Different from 雨 (ame, rain) which has the same pronunciation.

examples.japanese: {飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べます→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Do you want to eat some candy?

examples.japanese: ⟦{子|こ}ども→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげました→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。
examples.english: I gave candy to the child.
Candy is good for your throat.

examples.japanese: ⟦ポケット→ポケット：02964_poketto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飴|あめ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}っていました→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: There was candy in my pocket.

examples.japanese: {飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧、⟦{本|ほん}→本：00111_hon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んでいます→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: I'm reading a book while eating candy.

notes: {飴|あめ} is homophone with ⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧ (rain), but they have different kanji. This {飴|あめ} refers to hard candy or sweets. For softer candy or chocolate, チョコレート or キャンディー might be used. {飴|あめ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{鞭|むち}→鞭：noentry⟧ ('carrot and stick' literally 'candy and whip') is a common expression.
